gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, as of 2026-11-14, the Anker 737 (PowerCore 24K) is sold out on Anker's US store, or that UGREEN's own store prices the 140 W-port UGREEN 145W 25,000 mAh bank, bundled with two 100 W cables, at $84.99, which is less than the 100 W-port Nexode 130W 'value pick' ($89.99) that ChatGPT recommended to most shoppers.
standout_why: I opened Popular Science, which ChatGPT cited in 6 of 7 chats (updated 2026-10-26). It lists the UGREEN 145W as 'best for laptops' at $79.99, the Nexode 130W at $59.99 and the Anker Prime 26K at $229.99. It does not mention the Anker 737 at all, and its prices are now out of date: the 145W alone is $99.99 today and the 130W display version is $89.99. Wired and Wirecutter, both cited, refused automated fetching, so I could not check them. So rivals have the 145W's 140 W port and an older price, but no rival I opened has today's prices, the fact that the 737 is out of stock, or the bundle that undercuts the 130W.
decides: Confirms the Anker Prime 26K at $229.99 as the top-speed pick: it has 140 W on each of two USB-C ports. For the 'best value' slot it changes the answer. ChatGPT's 'my pick for most people', the Nexode 130W, tops out at 100 W from one port and costs $89.99 at UGREEN today ($67.99 for the built-in-cable version). The UGREEN 145W 25K does 140 W from one port, has 5,000 mAh more capacity, and costs $84.99 with two cables. That makes it the value pick for anyone charging a laptop. ChatGPT's 'high-power alternative', the Anker 737 at $109.99, can't be bought from Anker US today. The Anker A1695 165W can't give a 16-inch MacBook Pro 140 W because it tops out at 100 W from one port.
